decisions.reason: The effect is already fully represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY adding the SK6812 LEDs to the standalone 3.3V rail.
Moving the SK6812 LEDs to 3.3V necessarily removes them from the switchable 5V boost loads and makes the 5V LED standby policy obsolete.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The LEDs are now powered from 3.3V instead of 5V. At 3.3V supply the SK6812 data threshold drops to 2.31V, which the ESP32 3.3V output satisfies directly, so no level shifter is needed. The tradeoff is that 3.3V is slightly below the SK6812 datasheet minimum (3.7V), but it works reliably at indicator brightness levels.

decisions.reason: Both 3.3V and 5V rails remain monitored, and the existing downstream-current coverage remains valid without a state change.
The AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source for all system loads; only the downstream rail used by the LEDs changes.
The charge-status interface already specifies the SK6812 chain at 3.3V, so its current state remains valid unchanged.
The interboard interface still carries both 3.3V and 5V; changing the LED load assignment does not alter its connectors or routes.
The candidate already has a complete same-message MODIFY for the 3.3V supply, direct ESP32 data drive, accepted voltage constraint, and removal of the obsolete level-shifter part.
The LED supply and data-interface decision does not change the panel power-button connector or PWRON behavior.
The USB data interface and standalone programming behavior remain unchanged by the LED rail decision.
The LED rail decision does not affect battery cutoff thresholds or electrical protection behavior.
The LED rail decision does not affect the battery NTC connector or thermal-protection behavior.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY recording the 3.3V supply and accepted below-datasheet voltage constraint; data-level shifting belongs to the separate LED interface Requirement.
